title: Predicate evaluation failure handling — Layer 3 rule engine
closure_line: JOURNAL 1 LAYER 3 OPEN-L3-2 CLOSED — PREDICATE EVALUATION FAILURE SEMANTICS EXPLICITLY GOVERNED
selected_policy: Model C + Model D — three-valued predicate semantics with episode-level refusal

predicate_domain_semantics.TRUE: Antecedent predicate successfully evaluated and satisfied
predicate_domain_semantics.FALSE: Antecedent predicate successfully evaluated and not satisfied
predicate_domain_semantics.ERROR: Antecedent could not be established — evaluation failed

rule_firing_condition: A rule fires if and only if ALL predicates in its condition set evaluate to TRUE. Neither FALSE nor ERROR triggers rule firing.
error_unknown_semantics: ERROR/UNKNOWN means the antecedent could not be established. The rule does not fire. The episode enters evaluation_failure state and returns AI(E) = ∅. ERROR is not reinterpreted as FALSE and does not trigger rule firing.

episode_level_behaviour.human_authority: preserved — AI(E) = ∅ does not constrain human decision
episode_level_behaviour.trace_emission: trace always emitted with evaluation_failure = True; failed_rule_ids; failure_category

other_rules_may_continue_rationale: Episode-level refusal: once any predicate evaluation failure is detected, AI(E) = ∅ for the episode. No partial advisory output is produced. This is consistent with the existing ConfigurationError → AI(E) = ∅ pattern (OPEN-B3-1). The implementation may either abort on first failure or complete evaluation of all rules before refusing advisory generation; either implementation produces the same episode-level outcome.
s_mutation_policy: S is never mutated by Layer 3. A predicate evaluation failure does not change S, G(S), or A_AI(S). Layer 3 has no mechanism to modify S; that is exclusively Layer 2 / Algorithm 1 responsibility.

conceptual_fields_required.semantics: True if and only if any predicate evaluation failure occurred this episode. False if all predicates evaluated without error (regardless of whether rules fired).
conceptual_fields_required.purpose: Distinguishes evaluation_failure episodes from normal no-fire episodes in F1–F3 analysis.

conceptual_fields_required.semantics: Rule IDs of rules that experienced predicate evaluation failures. At minimum contains the first failed rule; ideally all failed rules if implementation continues evaluation after first failure.
conceptual_fields_required.purpose: Enables identification of which rules had predicate failures; supports debugging without confusing with quarantine (Model E, which is not selected).

conceptual_fields_required.semantics: Classification of the failure from the taxonomy: PREDICATE_EXCEPTION | NUMERIC_CONVERSION_FAILURE | MALFORMED_VALUE | INTERNAL_ERROR. None if no failure occurred.
conceptual_fields_required.purpose: Enables analysis of failure types without re-running episodes.

trace_requirements.key_distinguishability_requirement: fired_rule_ids = [] combined with evaluation_failure = False means all rules evaluated and none fired (normal no-fire). fired_rule_ids = [] combined with evaluation_failure = True means episode was aborted due to predicate evaluation failure. These MUST be distinguishable without inspection of any other field.
trace_requirements.configuration_failure_vs_evaluation_fail: configuration_failure (existing field) records Algorithm 3 / startup failures. evaluation_failure (new conceptual field) records runtime predicate evaluation failures. Both produce AI(E) = ∅ but at different stages for different reasons. Both must be in the trace.

extended_validation_scope.check: V1 — referenced variable exists in DecisionContext schema
extended_validation_scope.note: Prerequisite check: a variable with an unknown name has no type to check. Must precede V2.

extended_validation_scope.check: V2 — predicate operand/value type is compatible with the declared variable type
extended_validation_scope.note: Type compatibility is checkable from rule schema and context schema at supply time.

extended_validation_scope.check: V3 — predicate operator is valid for the declared variable/value operand types
extended_validation_scope.note: Operator validity depends on declared types, not runtime values.

extended_validation_scope.check: V4 — categorical predicate value belongs to the declared variable domain
extended_validation_scope.note: Value domains are defined in appendix-c; membership is checkable at supply time.

algorithm3_boundary.extended_validation_handling: Violations → ConfigurationError; configuration_failure = True in trace; AI(E) = ∅; S unchanged
algorithm3_boundary.authority_class: DESIGN_INTERPRETATION — extension of existing Algorithm 3 structural-validation role; no external authority explicitly requires this extension, but it is the natural boundary for structure-detectable vs. runtime-only failures
algorithm3_boundary.what_algorithm3_cannot_catch: Failures that depend on runtime context values — the actual observations in E at the time of reasoning

what_engine_reason_handles: Numeric conversion failures on actual context values (F-T-08)
algorithm4_boundary.engine_reason_contract_on_failure: Returns evaluation_failure = True (via EpisodeResult or equivalent); AI(E) = ∅; S unchanged. Does not rethrow the exception to the caller without producing a trace.
algorithm4_boundary.authority_class: DESIGN_INTERPRETATION — consistent with existing EpisodeResult contract and ConfigurationError → AI(E) = ∅ pattern
algorithm4_boundary.pseudocode_note: engine.reason(E, RS) at line 5 of Algorithm 4 now has a specified failure contract: any predicate evaluation failure → returns ∅ with evaluation_failure recorded. The gate-off at lines 1–3 is unaffected.

unsafe_behaviour.description: G(UNSAFE) = 0. Algorithm 4 lines 1–3 return AI = ∅ before engine.reason() is called. No rule set is selected for UNSAFE. No predicate evaluation occurs. OPEN-L3-2 policy is unreachable for UNSAFE episodes.

A_fail_closed.stop_condition: §14 — selected policy requires silently treating ERROR as FALSE
reasons: ERROR silently collapsed to FALSE; trace cannot distinguish evaluation failure from genuine no-fire.
Batch 1 Repair 3 explicitly removed the condition-evaluates-to-false assumption.
F1–F3 analysis would miscount evaluation failures as rule no-fires.

B_fail_open.stop_condition: §14 — selected policy can generate advisory from unestablished antecedent
reasons: Rule fires despite unestablished antecedent predicate.
Advisory generated without scientific basis — violates engine fidelity assumption P4.
Not consistent with any existing authority.

CE_rule_quarantine.stop_condition: None explicitly triggered; rejected on scientific defensibility grounds
reasons: Partial advisory (e.g. a hazard dimension not evaluated) may appear complete to the human fisher.
No existing authority in the repository supports partial advisory production on evaluation failure.
Inconsistent with ConfigurationError → AI(E) = ∅ pattern; introduces an asymmetry without justification.

With current RS_candidate structure (multiple independent CAUTION rules), a quarantined wave-assessment rule could leave the Delay recommendation appearing complete when one hazard dimension was not evaluated.

scientific_consequences.F1_type_compliance: Evaluation failure episodes return AI(E) = ∅, which trivially satisfies F1 (∅ ⊆ A_AI(S)). F1 analysis must separately count and report evaluation_failure episodes; they must not be folded into the general no-fire count.
scientific_consequences.F2_violation_count: Same as F1: evaluation failure episodes produce zero violations trivially. F2 analysis must separately label these episodes.
scientific_consequences.F3_RS_consistency: Unaffected. RS(S) is still selected by Algorithm 3 and corresponds to S. The failure occurs within engine.reason(), not at rule-set selection.
scientific_consequences.safety_dominance: AI(E) = ∅ ⊆ A_AI(S) for all S. Theorem C.3 holds for failure episodes. The fail-safe orientation is consistent.
scientific_consequences.rule_firing_interpretation: fired_rule_ids = [] must not be interpreted as all rules evaluated and none fired. In failure episodes it means rule evaluation was interrupted or aborted. The evaluation_failure field is the distinguishing marker.
scientific_consequences.advisory_completeness: AI(E) = ∅ on evaluation failure does not mean no actionable conditions were detected. The presentation layer must clearly distinguish evaluation_failure episodes (where AI(E) = ∅ means inability to evaluate) from normal SAFE episodes with no rules firing (where AI(E) = ∅ means all conditions assessed and no advisory triggered).
scientific_consequences.e5_latency: Failure-abort episodes have a different latency profile than successful reasoning. E5 analysis should separately identify and label evaluation_failure episodes rather than folding them into the general performance distribution.
